I think I understand now. The logic in using a vector of components is to implicitly (throughout the rest of the module) implement the merging logic detailed at https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/organize-cluster-access-kubeconfig/#merging-kubeconfig-files

I'm not sure I'm a fan of having things spread out like this. Perhaps the move is to put the logic for implementing the merge procedure into `get_kube_ctx_components`? Right now, I think if you have incomplete context components e.g. one config that only defines a user, and another config that only defined the namespace, the module will incorrectly only pick up on the first one defined.

Also surprisingly, it seems we don't actually have a test case for config merging.

I actually think it's now correct: 

> Never change the value or map key. Example: Preserve the context of the first file to set current-context. Example: If two files specify a red-user, use only values from the first file's red-user. Even if the second file has non-conflicting entries under red-user, discard them.

My reading is, that the last sentence implies that the first context found is used for everything, no matter if another config defines "non-conflicting" items (eg. your example: "one config that only defines a user, and another config that only defined the namespace").

Huh, I guess that's right. (And we did get [a comment](https://github.com/starship/starship/pull/3569#issuecomment-1102130317) that it wasn't working properly, though I don't really know what the issue was).
